children: China's new mortgage subsidy is likely to have limited practical impact, according to BofA Securities in a research note. While the subsidy could lower buyer's borrowing cost, the eligibility is "relatively narrow," the bank says. It points out that the subsidy applies only to newly issued commercial mortgages for first-home purchases, with qualifying properties capped at 120 square meters and 1.5 million yuan in value. That said, BofA thinks policy may still help to improve sentiment and provide a partial cushion against the constrained developer cash flow and property investment, the bank says. (tracy.qu@wsj.com)
